pamphlet_excerpts: Roles: PAs are health care providers who are licensedto diagnose and treat illness and disease and to prescribemedication for patients.
They Work Physician: They work in physician offices, hospitals and clinics in collaboration with a licensed physician.
PAs Work Primary: PAs work in primary care, sub-specialty care, and surgicalcare.
Roles PAs Advanced: The roles of PAs and Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (APRNs) are very similar (see the APRN section onpage 30), although their educational pathway.
step_by_step_procedure: States Formal: In most states, the PA must have a formal workingarrangement with a physician in order to practice.
Undergraduate Education: Undergraduate education in a variety ofscience/health disciplines will prepare thestudent for the graduate program.
PAprograms Require Applicant: Some PAprograms will require the applicant to havehad some experience in a health care setting.
Practice settings: Hospital, outpatientclinics, community health clinics, private practices, and prisons.

pamphlet_excerpts: Roles: These technicians make appliances such as artificiallimbs or braces.
Education: There is no specific college program for thisspecialty; rather training is on the job.
They Likely Wouldwork: They most likely wouldwork under the supervision of an orthotist or prosthetist whowould design the artificial limb, brace or removable splint.
Professionalsperform Imaging: These professionalsperform imaging of patients using a variety of techniques.
step_by_step_procedure: They Provide Radiation: They may also provide radiation therapy treatments.
Radiologic Technologists: Radiologic Technologists work directly withphysicians who are radiologists.
Education: Courses include anatomy, radiologictechniques, patient positioning, equipment protocols, radiationphysics and radiation safety as well as basic patient care.
Technologists Require: Radiologic Technologists require four-year bachelor’s degreesand Technicians require a two-year associate degree.
